recipient: Kenya Digital Transformation Center (via GIZ)
title: BMZ (Germany) - Kenya Digital Transformation Center (via GIZ): Digital Transformation Center Kenya
description: Context: In Africa, Kenya is considered a pioneer of digital transformation. Already many people use smartphones and the internet. An active start-up ecosystem and the growing field of IT services are creating new opportunities. Business process outsourcing (BPO) encourages innovation and employment. Nonetheless, many people lack digital skills and there is a need for clear rules governing data protection, competition and inclusion. Objective: Kenya has a sustainable and human-centred digital economy and society. Approach: The project expands the capacities of Kenyan public authorities and businesses to enable inclusive digital development. In addition, it promotes more dialogue between the state, the private sector and civil society.At the same time, it supports the establishment of digital public infrastructures (DPI) that facilitate access to digital services and help people to use them with confidence. The project focuses on promoting the BPO sector as a key motor for creating high-quality, formal jobs, in particular for young people and women, and as a driver of export-oriented digital services.The close cooperation between Kenyan and German technology and service companies opens up opportunities for both sides: Kenya benefits from knowledge transfer, investments and new jobs, Germany gains reliable partners for digital services, more stable supply chains and impulses for innovation from East Africa.The project is co-financed by the European Union (EU). This enhances the regional and international cooperation, and promotes partnerships between Europe and Africa. The target groups are political decision-makers, businesses and civil-society organisations, including Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPD).

recipient: Atlas Tower Kenya Limited
title: ATK Debt II — Atlas Tower Kenya mobile tower expansion
description:
The proposed transaction is a multi-currency senior debt financing of up to US$30 million, including an IFC A Loan of up to US$20 million and remaining to be mobilized from a B Lender/parallel lender for Atlas Tower Kenya (ATK or the Company), an IFC client since 2021. The funding will (i) enable ATK to build and operate new macro towers in Kenya, expanding its existing portfolio of 442 towers; (ii) support ATK's Green Power Program which involves the large-scale deployment of solar power, battery storage, and off-grid or hybrid energy solutions to help reduce dependence on grid electricity and diesel; and (iii) refinance existing indebtedness (Project). ATK is an independent telecommunications infrastructure company operating in Kenya under a build-to-suit (BTS) model. Established in 2018, ATK owns and operates a portfolio of 442 towers and manages the full tower lifecycle, including site identification, land leasing, permitting, construction, energy solutions, and operations and maintenance.

The most significant expected project-level outcome is to increase the capacity of mobile networks in Kenya, resulting in improved access to quality connectivity for individuals and businesses. Beyond the project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will deepen the competitiveness of the mobile tower market in Kenya by expanding shared infrastructure integrating green power solutions via competition channels.

recipient: Government of Kenya, Ministry of Health
title: U.S. Department of State — Kenya health data systems under the America First Global Health Strategy Cooperation Framework, 2025
description:
Paragraph 2.5.9.1 of the *Cooperation Framework between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of Kenya on Health*: "The U.S. Government intends to provide $175,000,000 over the course of the Framework to support data systems. The Government of Kenya intends to continue investing in the Digital Superhighway."

Appendix 1 gives the annual split of the data-systems line: **US$30,000,000 (2026), US$75,000,000 (2027), US$50,000,000 (2028), US$10,000,000 (2029), US$10,000,000 (2030)** — US fiscal years, 15 October to 30 September.

Paragraph 2.5.9.2–2.5.9.3 states the named uses: Kenya's **TaifaCare HMIS** enhancement including laboratory and pharmacy integration and scale-up and the onboarding of standalone systems; the **National Logistics Management System (NLMIS)** including its pharmacy module, track-and-trace and health commodity inventory management; **Kenya's surveillance systems including EOC digitization** and the outbreak response data system; one comprehensive **Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS)**; **KEMSA iLMIS and GS1 implementation**; and **Kenya's national and county data banks as its national and county health data warehouse**. Paragraph 2.5.9.4 records that the amount covers developers, product managers and systems engineers, cloud computing capacity and software licences, and hardware. Paragraph 2.5.9.5 leaves ongoing licensing, cloud, and hardware maintenance and replacement costs not specifically paid by the US Government to Kenya.

recipient: Mzalendo Trust
title: Mzalendo Trust — digital literacy, online safety and technology-facilitated GBV, Kenya
description: The project seeks to enhance the capacity of youth, women, and people with disabilities living in informal settlements on digital literacy and safety, and to enable civic education and awareness raising on Technology-Facilitated Gender Based Violence (TFGBV) through digital civic spaces. A growing area of concern in Kenya, TFGBV has far-reaching impacts on the rights, safety, and participation of individuals in digital and offline spaces, particularly women and girls. The 2022 General Elections in Kenya saw a dramatic increase in GBV (including TFGBV), and as the 2027 General Elections in Kenya approach, this project is timely and needed to support inclusive online civic engagement and to support the prevention of TFGBV amongst marginalised communities.Targeting informal settlements in Nairobi, Kiambu, Machakos, and Kajiado counties, this project will directly support communities most at risk and vulnerable to digital abuse in the lead up to the 2027 Elections, and learnings from this project can be shared with the Embassy’s other partners working on youth and women civic engagement.

description: One of the challenges facing businesses in kenya is finding qualified workers with specialist IT skills. The skills shortage is particularly acute in the areas of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) technologies such AI, Data Science, Computer Vision, Virtual reality, Augmented Reality, Blockchain, Space Tech and others. To address this skills shortage and fortify the local IT sector, my project seeks collaboration with the Frontiers community of experts. The initiative aims to establish and execute a program called ''Revolutionize Engineering'' enabling Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) as well as university students in Kenya to acquire expertise in 4IR technologies through a series of hackathons and makerthons.Revolutionize Engineering is a transformative one-year project, with a goal of establishing a community of 10,000 passionate engineering students in Africa, particularly in Kenya, focusing on emerging Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) technologies. title: COMMUNITY GRANT KENYA 2
description: Talent Forge is a digital collaborative network of Lif community members and engineering talent pipeline dedicated to propelling Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) technology solutions to tackle sustainability challenges in Kenya. Bringing together individuals, entrepreneurs, companies, and universities, the platform places a strong emphasis on fostering collaboration and community support. Within this network, every Kenyan LIF participant is committed to giving back to the engineering community by assisting Kenyan students, with a specific focus on women in STEM, in overcoming challenges and advancing in their Fourth Industrial Revolution careers or as innovators. Participants earn network points for their contributions, which can be exchanged for valuable services, exposure, and mentorship opportunities. This approach aims to empower and support women in STEM, creating a pathway for their success in the evolving landscape of 4IR technologies.Despite Africa's vast potential, women face significant underrepresentation in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) fields, particularly in Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) technologies such as AI, data science, Virtual Reality, Space tech IoT, industrial internet of things, cloud computing, cognitive computing, and blockchain. This disparity impedes Africa's ability to fully harness the transformative potential of these technologies, as global studies indicate that only 26% of tech jobs are held by women, with an even lower representation in Africa. UNESCO reports that a mere 35% of STEM students in Sub-Saharan Africa are female.Talent Forge is dedicated to bridging the gender gap by empowering over 300 female students with a strong interest in engineering from Kenyan universities, high schools, and TVETs. The initiative unfolds through a transformative three-week program, culminating in the Lif Community Innovation Day, conducted in collaboration with the Kenyan Lif community. This comprehensive program is meticulously designed to enhance skills in a broad spectrum of Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) technologies, including AI, data science, blockchain, virtual reality, augmented reality, computer vision, and space tech.The climax on the Lif Community Innovation Day adds a significant dimension to the initiative, providing a dynamic platform for showcasing and celebrating the innovative outcomes of the program. It also serves as a moment to highlight and celebrate success stories within the Lif community, illustrating their impactful contributions to tackling sustainability challenges in Kenya. This inclusive approach emphasizes not only skill development but also the collective achievements and advancements made by the Lif community in addressing critical issues in the country.In partnership with emerging tech companies from the Lif Community in Kenya, Talent Forge establishes pathways for female students to access job opportunities and apply their skills to address global challenges. This initiative recognizes the pivotal role of emerging technologies in Africa's future and aims to equip young women to become leaders in shaping the continent's 4IR landscape.As an integral part of the project, the three-week program that will be conducted in Kenya, offers a unique opportunity for female students to engage in hands-on learning, drawing inspiration from the Lif community's experience. This immersive experience encourages innovation around various 4IR technologies, fostering collaboration and skill development.

title: Exploring the private-sector role in the Sustainable Development Goal data revolution
description: The private sector is already playing a role in providing data to support social and economic development in developing countries. In Sri Lanka and Colombia, call detail records have been used to predict population-level socio-economic characteristics and displacement after natural disasters. In sub-Saharan Africa and India, Facebook and other social-media data have been used to map the population and provide alternative data to predict credit scores to expand financial inclusion.   Since the announcement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the calls for a 'data revolution for sustainable development,' the private sector has been asked to commit to partnering with the public sector in achieving the SDGs. Calls for private-sector actions such as data sharing and capacity building to assist in monitoring and achieving the SDGs were met by public commitments by the private sector. The need for private-sector participation is even more critical in developing countries, where most public statistical systems are less developed and institutions have lower capacity. In order to catalyze responsible private-sector participation in data for sustainable development, this project will explore the extent of private-sector participation and how it has contributed to the data revolution, how the private sector is contributing to good data-governance practices, and the challenges the private sector, governments and civil societies face in attempting to come together and use multiple sources of data. title: Sat4Wildlife ecosystem of Geospatial Intelligence tools to protect wildlife & habitats
description: The Sat4Wildlife project strives to reduce threats to Kenya's species and habitats and improve climate resilience through the application of satellite enabled technology that can inform conservation actions in a timely and efficient manner.  The use of satellite enabled technology to support conservation management is growing, and the potential is great, however there remain limitations in its application. Challenges exist around connectivity, cost of technology and ongoing maintenance, end user capacity to identify and effectively use technology solutions, and there is limited interoperability between different technology solutions making it hard to gain a holistic picture and effectively respond to multiple data streams about conservation critical activities. All of these factors impact how sustainable technology solutions are and therefore their lasting value to conservation.  The Discovery Phase of the project worked to understand in more detail the specific challenges faced by the different user groups in Kenya and to design an ecosystem which could help meet these needs and create a lasting impact in country. The final outcomes expected if the project continues include conservation actors being better able to predict and respond to the effects of climate variability as well as HWC and illegal wildlife trade.  To achieve these outcomes the project plans to establish a Centre of Excellence at the Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Kenya. This takes the form of a physical site for collaborative testing and developing of technologies and a programme of training and convening of cross sector events to support learning and knowledge sharing.  Alongside this, the existing WILDLABS platform will be rescoped and scaled to create a go- to platform for information, collaboration and learning across the global conservation tech community. Underpinning both the Centre of Excellence and the WILDLABS platform is a series of strategic activities (WILDLABS Programmes) as well as a series of Capacity Building activities to grow skills and knowledge and increase community networks across the country.  Within the WILDLABS Platform a distribution pipeline will be created to provide users with a streamlined service to aid procurement and logistics of hardware in Kenya and help to unlock access for purchasing and acquiring new conservation technologies.  The bringing together of the WILDLABS Platform and Programmes, and distribution pipeline with the Centre of Excellence and programme of capacity development creates an ecosystem of tools to address the challenges identified in country and leads to the final impact of mitigating the risk to Kenyan wildlife, enhancing the conservation of biodiversity and improving climate resilience.

title: Registering Births and Deaths in Kenya: Current problems, solution pathways and interventions.
description: The lack of reliable, timely data on deaths (who, when, what) and births in SSA continues to pose a considerable challenge to estimating intervention needs. Many events across Africa remain invisible to national and international health metrics and health system planners. Informed health policy requires reliable descriptions of births and the age, sex and causes of death for the entire population. New context-specific evidence is required to understand the challenges that plague CRVS systems in Africa. I will use a network of surveillance sites in Kenya to answer four related questions: a) What and where are the gaps and inefficiencies in the current civil registration processes? b) What is the true proportion of unregistered births and deaths in Kenya? c) do individuals have the same probability of being registered by CRVS when they are born or when they die? and d) Why are some births or deaths not registered and are these events systematically different, and what are the potential opportunities and strategies to strengthen registration of all children. This body of work will inform the design of an intervention package aimed at improved monitoring of changes in mortality and natality and demonstrate how to achieve comprehensive CRVS in Kenya

title: Developing responsible African AI policy environments: Policy Centre II
description: The aim of this initiative is to ensure that policymakers have access to timely, high-quality policy research to support decision-making on responsible artificial intelligence (AI) policy issues. It will support a policy research agenda for Eastern Africa that explores how to enable and implement responsible AI that is developed and implemented to be ethical, rights-based, inclusive, and sustainable. This project will enhance the capacity of policymakers, technologists, and business leaders to take on the challenges of AI, improve their processes and outputs related to responsible AI, and create a framework for AI innovation. It will identify and investigate the societal benefits, risks, and harms associated with AI deployment in the pan-African context and offer proposals on pre-empting or mitigating negative effects and maximizing positive outcomes. It will also develop a set of context-appropriate resources on responsible AI for use in digital policymaking and technical and professional training, including policy guidance to navigate the technical, legal, social, and ethical challenges of AI-based systems. It will collaborate with specialists across disciplines to help develop transdisciplinary research, increase gender awareness, and enhance the adoption and implementation of responsible AI policy by local and regional governments. This project is supported through the Artificial Intelligence for Development in Africa (AI4D) program, a joint investment from IDRC and the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, which focuses on three main pillars: capacity strengthening and amplifying AI talent and communities in Africa, supporting rights and inclusion through the development of responsible AI policy, and advancing AI innovation networks to address Africa's development challenges.

title: NRF - No Marginalization in Digitization (Kenya)
description: As Kenya moves rapidly towards a new digital ID and population register, which threatens to restrict access to services, increase data protection risks, and exclude communities facing discrimination in access to documentation, the rights of all Kenyans are at stake. Communities at risk for further exclusion must engage in the political process to ensure the transition to digital identity is an opportunity to right past wrongs rather than entrench discriminatory, unequal treatment. recipient: KEN; International Development Research Centre; Strathmore University, named as transaction receiver
title: Strengthening cyber policy research centres in the Global South – Centre for Intellectual Property and Information Technology Law
description: Networking technologies are increasingly at the heart of economic, social, and political activities. Although they facilitate new opportunities, networking and communication tools can also introduce vulnerabilities — such as surveillance, tracking, censorship, and repression — that require new standards, skills, and applications. With the amplification of technology’s role in economic and political empowerment, policy and regulation are key to ensure that its harms are restricted. Leaders and policymakers generally lack the evidence and objective advice to develop effective regulation in the digital space, yet they are increasingly confronted with cyber threats (crime, terrorism) and other challenges, such as how to govern and support artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystems. Policymakers in the Global South need to ensure that unstable or insecure digital environments do not undermine potential, and that their policies and regulations can adequately respond to new digital challenges such as AI. Furthermore, they must balance a range of priorities with obligations to protect privacy and free expression. The complexity of cyber-related issues such as AI and data governance requires integrated policies that incorporate expertise and approaches from overlapping areas, including telecommunications and infrastructure, economics, technology, law, and other social sciences — but there are few organizations or experts in the Global South that specifically research cyber policy issues. This initiative is helping to strengthen research and policy capacity on critical digital policy issues to ensure that policymakers in the Global South consistently use objective, high quality research to inform digital policy development. Centres will be supported to develop a robust policy research agenda that addresses all facets of cyber and digital policy, including human rights, security, and innovation, and the interplay of these issues in the Global South. It will help build institutional capacity and sustainability to produce credible, legitimate, and locally-relevant research that convenes different perspectives on critical policy issues, and it will strengthen the capacity of centres to inform and influence policy development. Together, this will enable policy leaders to respond to the rapidly changing digital environment and allow communities to benefit from the opportunities that digital innovation offers, including improved health, governance, education, and economic prospects, while shielding them as much as possible from the harms.

title: Strengthening the management and sharing of research data
description: Governments, research funders, scholarly publishers, and academic organizations are increasingly advocating for greater openness to research data to catalyze innovation and collaboration and to uphold research integrity by allowing others to query or build on research findings. While these rationales are compelling, the management, curation, and archiving of research data in open repositories is not established practice in Asia, Africa, and Latin America. This project seeks to strengthen the management and sharing of research data generated through IDRC-funded research projects. The project will invite researchers funded by IDRC to participate in a peer-learning process that will result in their data being archived in appropriate data repositories. This will involve the development of data management plans, papers describing their data, and the curation of datasets. The process will be guided by international advisors who will help researchers understand the administrative process, ethical considerations, and data curation techniques that support the archiving of research data in open repositories. As researcher practices and infrastructures vary across regions, the project will convene workshops in Africa, Asia, and South America to exchange experiences in the management and sharing of research data in each region. Insights from peer exchanges and guidance provided by the international advisors will be used by researchers to publish their data papers and archive their data. IDRC staff will contribute to and learn from these peer-learning processes to improve the guidance the Centre provides to grantees in support of its Open Data Statement of Principles.
